In Android, you can use the `Navigation` component to navigate between different activities in your app. To use the `Navigation` component, you will need to set up a navigation graph, which is a set of activities and their transitions. The navigation graph is defined in a file called `navigation.xml` or `navigation.json`, which you can place in the `app/src/navigation` directory of your app.

Here is an example of how you can define a navigation graph in `navigation.xml`:
```php
<navigation xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:app="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res-auto"
    xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools"
    app:startDestination="@id/home">

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/home"
        android:name="com.example.myapp.HomeFragment"
        android:label="home" />

    <fragment
        android:id="@+id/settings"
        android:name="com.example.myapp.SettingsFragment"
        android:label="settings" />

    <action
        android:id="@+id/action_home_to_settings"
        app:destination="@id/settings"
        android:label="settings" />

</navigation>
```
In this example, we have defined two fragments, `HomeFragment` and `SettingsFragment`, and a transition between them. The `startDestination` attribute specifies which fragment should be launched when the app starts. The `action` element defines a transition from the `HomeFragment` to the `SettingsFragment`, which can be triggered by clicking a button or some other user action.

```java

```
